name: Spicy Vodka Rigatoni with Italian Sausage
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Creamy tomato pasta with a heat angle the catalog does not have on the pork side. Both flags are optional: red-pepper-flakes (tracked) replaces the Calabrian chilis and the vodka can be omitted entirely without changing the sauce meaningfully. Distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers (cream-and-tomato-paste sauce, no bell peppers, rigatoni). CONFIDENCE: the source page publishes no nutrition data at all, so est_cal and the protein claim are both projected from the ingredient list, not verified. | HARVEST: Source states 4-6 servings; midpoint 5 recorded. No nutrition data published.
intro_html: Vodka sauce is really just tomato paste cooked until it goes brick red, then softened with cream. We build it exactly that way and skip the vodka entirely, because it does not change the sauce and it does not belong on a grocery list this tight. Hot Italian sausage, red pepper flakes, kale and short tube pasta, at 31 grams of protein for about $1.66.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (red pepper flakes, black pepper, salt): ~$1.00. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $23.24 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.66 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $29.54 across 14 servings, roughly $2.11 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $14.18 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $43.72. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.66 a bowl for a creamy, spicy pasta that reads like a restaurant plate. The pasta and the sauce base are pennies. The sausage and the cream are where the money goes.
shop_smart: Skip the vodka. It is the single most expensive optional ingredient in Italian American cooking and the sauce does not miss it. Cooking the tomato paste properly is what actually builds that flavor.
Store brand ziti or rigatoni, whichever is cheaper. Any short tube with ridges holds this sauce. Brand loyalty on dry pasta is money thrown away.
Heavy cream is the line to watch. It is the biggest non meat cost here. Evaporated milk will get you a lighter but still creamy sauce for considerably less.
Red pepper flakes replace the Calabrian chilis. The original calls for a specialty jarred chili. Flakes from your spice rack bring the same heat and cost nothing extra.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and strip the kale leaves from their stems and tear them.
Boil the pasta in well salted water until just shy of tender, then reserve a mug of the starchy water before you drain it. That water is what makes the sauce cling later.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles until it has color, not just gray.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic and the red pepper flakes for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and keep stirring for three or four minutes until it darkens from bright red to brick. This step is the whole sauce, so do not rush it.
Pour in the heavy cream, stir until it turns a uniform blush color, then fold in the torn kale and let it wilt.
Add the drained pasta and the parmesan, splash in the reserved pasta water a little at a time, and toss until the sauce coats every piece.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, tossing between scoops so the sausage does not settle to the bottom. Every bowl lands near 792 calories and 31 grams of protein.

head.description: Spicy creamy tomato pasta with hot Italian sausage, kale and parmesan, no vodka needed. 14 servings, 792 calories, 31g protein, about $1.66 each.
head.keywords: spicy vodka rigatoni, italian sausage pasta, creamy tomato pasta, spicy rigatoni, budget pasta meal prep
steps: Boil the pasta until just shy of tender and reserve a mug of the starchy cooking water.
Brown the hot Italian sausage in olive oil, then add the onion, garlic and red pepper flakes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it darkens to brick red.
Pour in the heavy cream and stir until the sauce turns blush, then wilt in the torn kale.
Add the pasta and parmesan and toss with reserved pasta water until the sauce coats everything.
